lines.text: From a night he hasn't lived yet.
[low, steady] Six days. That's all his last message gave him.
[dry, a little wry] And he'd left his umbrella behind in the rain.
[thinking it through, matter-of-fact] A receipt in the strap. Same bakery. Same order. Six-twenty, every morning.
lines.show: A receipt in the strap. Same bakery. Same order. 6:20, every morning.

lines.text: [dry, quietly certain] People who buy bread at the same hour every day don't live far from where they buy it.
[softly, a little amazed] You followed a bus in the rain. For an umbrella.
[simply, not backing down] Then it looked important.
[low, piecing it together] The name stitched inside the strap said Arjun. Not his, then.
[practical, kind] You're soaked. I'll make tea.
[polite, a little awkward] You don't have to.
[low, observing] Two mugs on the rack, one never used. A photograph, turned to face the wall.
[low, unsettled] He'd said that to me before. In a message. From a night he hasn't lived yet.
